document_assessment.summary: Sample output for a flat, finished-form annotation sheet profile.

batch_readiness.readiness_summary: The profile fixture preserves production pseudo-markers and therefore uses comments instead of direct marker-touching edits.

gates.finding: The fixture uses literal production pseudo-markers inside flat Word paragraphs.
gates.required_action: Do not apply direct edits that touch marker tokens.

gates.finding: Profile audit should preserve pseudo-markers and lexical unitization.

checks.finding: The front-matter unit is correctly preserved as context.
checks.standard: Finished-form FRUS annotation sheets may use flat Word styles; front matter should be identified by lexical structure.

checks.finding: The source note contains literal production pseudo-markers.
checks.standard: Production pseudo-markers should be preserved literally or mapped reversibly by the wrapper; uncertain marker handling should be comment-only.
checks.comment_text: Preserve the literal production pseudo-markers unless the closed-network wrapper maps them reversibly before redline application.

checks.finding: The lot-file source-list entry is correctly preserved as source-list context.
checks.standard: Lot-file rows can be plain paragraphs and should not be treated as transcribed document text.

style_discrepancy_tally.style_question: Whether production pseudo-markers should remain literal during closed-network review or be mapped to Word formatting before tracked changes.
style_discrepancy_tally.variant_a: Preserve literal markers and use comments when edits would touch them.
style_discrepancy_tally.variant_b: Map markers to Word formatting before review and back to publication tokens after review.
style_discrepancy_tally.general_editor_question: Should the closed-network checker standardize one reversible marker policy for finished annotation sheets?
